nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Coventry Cathedral and reconciliation today

nodes.misconception: Christian teaching on forgiveness is simply to forgive people the first time.
nodes.response: The teaching of Jesus on forgiveness was challenging at the time and challenging for Christians today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus' teaching about forgiveness

nodes.misconception: Desmond Tutu was only active during the apartheid era.
nodes.response: Desmond Tutu played a role after apartheid and was a lifelong campaigner for justice and reconciliation.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Reconciliation: the work of Desmond Tutu

nodes.misconception: Everyone welcomed Prophet Muhammad's message.
nodes.response: Prophet Muhammad faced opposition and persecution as not everyone welcomed his message.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Prophet Muhammad's challenges

nodes.misconception: The Prophet Muhammad taught his companions not to respect other beliefs.
nodes.response: The Prophet Muhammad taught to respect other beliefs such as Judaism and Christianity.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Prophet Muhammad the leader

nodes.misconception: The Qur'an was authored by the Prophet Muhammad.
nodes.response: Most Muslims believe that the Qur'an was revealed to Muhammad and is the word of God (Allah). The Hadith contain sayings of Muhammad collected by his companions.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The words of Prophet Muhammad today

nodes.misconception: The Prophet Muhammad was only concerned with spiritual matters.
nodes.response: The Prophet Muhammad taught about caring for the world and other people. These teachings and examples are followed by millions of Muslims today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Prophet Muhammad and care for the world

nodes.misconception: Arabia has always been Muslim.
nodes.response: Arabia was inhabited by Christians, Jews and people who had polytheistic beliefs before the time of Prophet Muhammad.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The childhood of Prophet Muhammad

nodes.misconception: Muhammad was always a religious man and prophet.
nodes.response: Muhammad was a merchant and a family man before he received his calling from God.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The early life of Prophet Muhammad

nodes.misconception: Humanists don't believe in anything.
nodes.response: Humanists do have beliefs! They believe in people, kindness, fairness, and making good choices. But they believe without faith in a god.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanist choices: The Fox and the Stork

nodes.misconception: Rules are there to stop us from doing things.
nodes.response: Many rules are designed to keep us safe.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Rules to live by

nodes.misconception: Moses made up the Ten Commandments himself.
nodes.response: Jewish people believe that God gave these special rules to Moses on a mountain.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Ten Commandments

nodes.misconception: Everyone believes in God.
nodes.response: Some people believe in God, and some people don’t. Everyone has their own way of thinking.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Reflecting on rules and choices

nodes.misconception: Dharma is about following a fixed set of rules.
nodes.response: Dharma is about doing what is right and so rules may need to be applied flexibly.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Dharma: Ganesha's race around the world

nodes.misconception: Jesus replaced the Ten Commandments as they were outdated.
nodes.response: Jesus summarised the Commandments with his call to love others.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus and good choices

nodes.misconception: That only religious people can be part of a group with others who share their values.
nodes.response: A person does not have to be religious to have values such as kindness.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Belonging as a humanist

nodes.misconception: That a person can only be part of one community.
nodes.response: We can belong to multiple communities, such as our family, school, faith or clubs.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: What does it mean to belong?

nodes.misconception: There is only one way to belong.
nodes.response: Belonging can look different in different places and with different people.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The idea of belonging

nodes.misconception: Some may think that you can only belong to a Christian faith family if you go to church every week.
nodes.response: Remind the children that Christians can belong to their faith family in different ways, such as praying at home, helping others, or praying to God. Going to church is one way, but not the only way.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christians and their faith family

nodes.misconception: The children may think that Shabbat is a once a year special event (for example, they might think it is similar to an event such as Christmas).
nodes.response: Remind the children that Shabbat happens every week and it is a shared part of Jewish life for the Jewish faith family across the world.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Shabbat: belonging to a Jewish family

nodes.misconception: All symbols are religious.
nodes.response: Some symbols represent a faith or belief, though not all members will choose these. There are many other symbols which are not religious and represent other groups or information.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Symbols of belonging

nodes.misconception: Jesus was a Christian.
nodes.response: Jesus was a Jew and followed Jewish traditions. Jesus celebrated the Pesach meal with his disciples.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Last Supper: different Christian interpretations

nodes.misconception: Christians only go to church on Easter Sunday to mark Easter.
nodes.response: Some Churches will hold services throughout Holy Week and Christians may go to a number of services.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Celebrating Holy Week: a case study

nodes.misconception: Christmas is the most important festival to Christians.
nodes.response: Easter is a more important festival to most Christians than Christmas.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Holy Week: significance to different Christians

nodes.misconception: Christians from different churches always disagree and never work together.
nodes.response: Christians from different churches often agree with each other and work together.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Good Friday: different Christian commemorations

nodes.misconception: There is just one account of the resurrection.
nodes.response: The Gospel accounts all recount that Jesus was raised from the dead and appeared to his disciples in slightly different versions.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The resurrection: different Gospel accounts

nodes.misconception: All Christians renew vows on Maundy Thursday.
nodes.response: Deacons, priests and bishops from the Church of England church renew their ordination vows on Maundy Thursday.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Maundy Thursday: other events

nodes.misconception: Nothing changes for children after their mitzvahs.
nodes.response: After their Bar or Bat Mitzvah, children take on new responsibilities and are seen as adults in their religion.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Bat Mitzvah and Bar Mitzvah today

nodes.misconception: Christians all celebrate the same ceremony to mark adulthood.
nodes.response: There are a variety of ceremonies different Christians might experience.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian rites of passage : confirmation and believer's baptism

nodes.misconception: Everybody marks the same stages in a person's life.
nodes.response: Different cultures and religions identify different stages. There are some similarities but also differences.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian rites of passage: baptism

nodes.misconception: Only Hindu boys have their Mundan haircut.
nodes.response: Both boys and girls can have their Mundan first haircut as part of this special tradition.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Welcoming a Hindu baby

nodes.misconception: Only boys have Bar Mitzvahs, and girls don’t have any special ceremony.
nodes.response: Both boys and girls have special ceremonies when they become responsible in Jewish tradition. In some Jewish groups, boys and girls celebrate a little differently, but both are very important and special!
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Bat Mitzvah and Bar Mitzvah

nodes.misconception: All religions mark the same rites of passage in the same way.
nodes.response: Different religions have different rituals and traditions that mark stages in a person's life from being welcomed as a baby to growing into an adult.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Similarities and differences in rites of passage

nodes.misconception: Only Roman Catholic Christians visit Jerusalem.
nodes.response: Christians from different traditions visit many places on pilgrimage. Jerusalem is the most sacred place as it is where Jesus was crucified and was raised from the dead.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jerusalem: a place of Christian pilgrimage

nodes.misconception: Jerusalem is only a place of pilgrimage for Jews.
nodes.response: Jews, Christians and Muslims go on pilgrimage to Jerusalem.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jerusalem: the site of the Jewish temple

nodes.misconception: A Muslim can go on Hajj whenever they choose.
nodes.response: Hajj is expensive, so people may well save up. Saudi Arabia operates a quota for each country.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Hajj: the impact on believers

nodes.misconception: The Hajj pilgrimage to Makkah is the only pilgrimage for Muslims.
nodes.response: Karbala is a place of pilgrimage for Shi'a Muslims. Jerusalem is also a place of pilgrimage for Muslims.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Karbala: a Shi'a place of pilgrimage

nodes.misconception: Only Muslims go on pilgrimage.
nodes.response: Many different religions have pilgrimage as a core belief.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The idea of pilgrimage

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that only men go on Hajj.
nodes.response: Men and Women may both go on Hajj. They might have different clothes to wear but will carry out the same actions.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Hajj: a sacred duty for Muslims

nodes.misconception: All Muslim women wear a hijab.
nodes.response: Some Muslim women wear a hijab whilst others do not. Many Muslim women feel wearing a hijab is an empowering element of their identity.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Dress and modesty for Muslims today

nodes.misconception: Muslims are all the same.
nodes.response: The Muslim community is highly diverse.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Diversity in the Muslim community today

nodes.misconception: Muslims have only lived in the UK since the 20th century.
nodes.response: Muslims have lived in the UK for many centuries though the population has increased in the last century.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslims in Britain today

nodes.misconception: All Muslim women stay at home and look after children.
nodes.response: Many Muslim women study at university and have highly successful careers as well as raising a family.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Belonging to a Muslim family

nodes.misconception: Zakat is just like giving to any charity.
nodes.response: Zakat is a specific type of giving that Muslims must do every year if they have enough wealth.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Charity and generosity

nodes.misconception: The UK is a safe and equal country, so Muslims do not suffer prejudice.
nodes.response: Many Muslims experience prejudice. Incidents of Islamophobia have increased in recent years.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Contributions and challenges

nodes.misconception: Caring is only within your family
nodes.response: Caring happens everywhere and with everyone
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Thought experiment: the idea of care

nodes.misconception: A neighbour is the person who lives next door to you.
nodes.response: Anyone outside of your family is a neighbour.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The story of the Good Samaritan

nodes.misconception: Christians only care for other Christians.
nodes.response: Many Christians care for others regardless of their worldview
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Good Samaritan:  Christian caring today

nodes.misconception: People who belong to a particular religion only help those from that same background.
nodes.response: Interfaith groups as well as religious and non-religious people can work together.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How faith can inspire others to care

nodes.misconception: Prayer is more important than caring for others.
nodes.response: Caring is as important as prayer.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The story of Muhammad and The Hungry Stranger

nodes.misconception: Muslims only care for other Muslims.
nodes.response: Muslims care for others regardless of religion or belief.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Hungry Stranger: Muslim caring today

nodes.misconception: Only Christians have a creation story about the six days.
nodes.response: The same story in the book of Genesis is shared by Jews and Christians.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The idea of beginnings

nodes.misconception: Christians and Jews all understand the creation story in the same way.
nodes.response: There are different ways to interpret and understand the creation stories in the Bible.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Creation: deeper meanings

nodes.misconception: The Muslim creation story is exactly the same as stories told by Jews and Christians.
nodes.response: There are some similar ideas about creation and some differences.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim ideas about creation

nodes.misconception: Humanists don’t think about about how the world began.
nodes.response: Humanists use ideas from science to ask and answer questions about how the world began.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanists and how the world started

nodes.misconception: People with religious and non-religious worldviews have completely different ideas about how the world began.
nodes.response: People with religious and non-religious worldview share some ideas about how the world began.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different ideas about origins of the world

nodes.misconception: The Bible and the Qur’an say that people are in charge so they can do what they like with the world.
nodes.response: Most Christians, Jews and Muslims believe they have a responsibility to care for the world.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Stewardship and care of the world

nodes.misconception: All worldviews have completely different ideas about how to live a good life.
nodes.response: Worldviews share some ideas, such as the Golden Rule.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Deciding what is a good life

nodes.misconception: The Qur’an is the only source of Muslim ethical teaching.
nodes.response: Muslims also follow the Sunnah to guide them into living a good life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim values

nodes.misconception: Philosophy is only for older, clever people.
nodes.response: Philosophy is about deep thinking - it is for everyone, including children.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Ethics and values

nodes.misconception: Christians all think the same way.
nodes.response: Christians might apply Jesus’ teaching in different ways.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian values

nodes.misconception: Philosophy is ancient and has no meaning for today.
nodes.response: Philosophy has its roots in Ancient Greece, but the ideas are still important today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Aristotle and the golden mean

nodes.misconception: Humanists make decisions based on what suits them personally.
nodes.response: Humanists use empathy to make a decision that helps as many people as possible.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanist values

nodes.misconception: People from different worldviews are only found in certain places.
nodes.response: People from different worldviews can be found in a variety of different places. Some localities have historical populations of people from a particular worldview. But the census shows that people are moving to different areas as well.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Changing context and worldviews in the UK

nodes.misconception: All religion is declining in the UK.
nodes.response: Christianity has declined in the UK, whilst other religions have increased. There are differences in different geographical contexts.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The census and worldviews in the UK

nodes.misconception: Only religious people have a worldview.
nodes.response: Everyone has a worldview. For some people it may be linked to a particular religion. For others it might be a non-religious worldview.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The concept of a worldview

nodes.misconception: Because Christianity is declining according to census data, there are no new churches being built in the UK.
nodes.response: New churches are still being built or converted from other buildings in the UK today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Changing worldviews in our community

nodes.misconception: Religions and worldviews will look the same in our local area compared to England and Wales.
nodes.response: Data may look similar or different. There may be local variations, meaning that your local data may be very similar or completely different to national data.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Investigating worldviews in our community

nodes.misconception: The majority of people in the world do not have a religious worldview.
nodes.response: The majority of people in the world have a religious worldview. Religion and belief varies around the world depending on context.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The global context of worldviews

nodes.misconception: Prayer only happens in a church.
nodes.response: Christians pray in churches but also in many other different places.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different Christian prayers

nodes.misconception: All prayer looks the same.
nodes.response: There are many different ways of praying.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Introducing prayer

nodes.misconception: There is only one version of the Lord's Prayer.
nodes.response: The Lord's Prayer is said in many different churches, at home and even in some schools. It has many translations from the original language, so can sound very different.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Lord's Prayer

nodes.misconception: Prayer and reflection has no value today.
nodes.response: People find it useful to pray and reflect to gain balance in their busy lives.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Comparing prayer and reflection

nodes.misconception: Only religious people reflect and meditate.
nodes.response: Many people value time to reflect and meditate whether they are religious or not.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanist reflection

nodes.misconception: Muslims only pray in the mosque for salat.
nodes.response: Muslims pray at home, in the mosque or any clean ground for salat.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different Muslim prayers

nodes.misconception: Ants are only insects and don't matter.
nodes.response: Prophet Muhammad taught that all living things should be cared for.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim stories: The Ants

nodes.misconception: Some problems are so big that you can't do anything about them.
nodes.response: Everyone can do at least one thing to make a difference.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The story of the Starfish Thrower

nodes.misconception: Stories are just told for fun.
nodes.response: Many stories have a deeper meaning that contains a message about life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Stories and deeper meanings

nodes.misconception: Animals are just for humans to use as they wish.
nodes.response: The Prophet Muhammad taught that we should be kind to all animals.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim stories: the Crying Camel

nodes.misconception: The only point of the parable is welcoming home the lost son.
nodes.response: The parable is about the father’s love and forgiveness for both his sons.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Parable of the Lost Son: hidden meanings

nodes.misconception: Jesus only taught stories to his followers that were simple to understand.
nodes.response: Sometimes Jesus told stories that contained a challenging message for the audience.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The story of the Lost Son

nodes.misconception: Christians only sing words from the Bible.
nodes.response: Christians sing words from the Bible, and other song lyrics based on their beliefs and experiences.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian words and music

nodes.misconception: All Christians use the same music styles.
nodes.response: Christians use music of many different styles in their worship.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different styles of Christian music

nodes.misconception: Muslims don’t compose or perform music for worship.
nodes.response: Some Muslims do compose or perform music to worship God (Allah).
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different Muslim approaches to music

nodes.misconception: Worship always involves talking or music.
nodes.response: Worship can be silent.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Stillness and silence

nodes.misconception: There are no musical sounds in Islamic ritual.
nodes.response: Recitation of the Qur’an and the call to prayer have cadence, melody and rhythm.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Recitation in Islam

nodes.misconception: Sikhs are not allowed to use music in their worship.
nodes.response: Music is an important element of Sikh worship at home and in the gurdwara.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Inspiration through music in Sikhi

nodes.misconception: We know what Jesus looked like. The white Jesus seen in stained glass windows is an authentic representation of Jesus.
nodes.response: We do not know what Jesus looked like. Artists all over the world can paint or represent Jesus from within their own cultures.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How Christians use art to show faith

nodes.misconception: Ony artistic people can produce art.
nodes.response: All people can produce art that represents their beliefs and values. This art can take many forms.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Design an artwork to express beliefs

nodes.misconception: Muslims do not use poetry to understand ideas of God.
nodes.response: Poetry is an art form that Muslims use as a way of expressing their beliefs.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Poetry and expressing feelings

nodes.misconception: Calligraphy is just pretty writing.
nodes.response: Calligraphy is an art form that communicates meaning.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Calligraphy and its importance to Muslims

nodes.misconception: All Christians view art in the same way.
nodes.response: There are differing Christian worldviews on the role of art. Some Christians use art as a form of devotion. Some, like many Orthodox Christians, venerate icons. Other Christians see art as distracting from a focus on God.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How Christians use art to tell stories

nodes.misconception: Words are the only way of explaining things.
nodes.response: People express thoughts and feelings in lots of different ways.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Symbols instead of words

nodes.misconception: Ceremonies are only marked by people who believe in god.
nodes.response: Humanists do not belive in god, but have ceremonies to mark meaningful events in life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanist ceremonies

nodes.misconception: Using empathy when making ethical decisions means that all humanists will reach the same conclusions.
nodes.response: Humanists may reach different moral decisions as they feel empathy differently.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanism: deciding right from wrong

nodes.misconception: The word humanism means that humanists are only interested in other humans.
nodes.response: Humanism is a worldview that see humans as part of the natural world. Humanists are concerned with all life on earth.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanism: a natural origin and a precious planet

nodes.misconception: A humanist belief in the one life means that they can do whatever they want.
nodes.response: A humanist belief in the one life motivates them to find meaning, purpose and happiness.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The one life

nodes.misconception: Humanists are only found in Europe and North America.
nodes.response: There are humanists all over the world, across all continents.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanism around the world

nodes.misconception: It isn't possible to live a meaningful life without religion.
nodes.response: Humanism is a non religious worldview, in which people can live a meangful life without religion.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Humanist beliefs

nodes.misconception: There is only one type of church. All churches have stained glass windows, towers and are made of stone.
nodes.response: Churches come in all shapes and sizes. Some look very traditional and some are modern.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How churches differ

nodes.misconception: All Jews wear a prayer shawl/tallit.
nodes.response: Jewish men wear a prayer shawl/tallit after the age of 13.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Belonging to an Orthodox synagogue

nodes.misconception: All mosques will look the same and have features such as a dome.
nodes.response: Mosques may be purpose-built or adapted. They may have some features such as domes or not. All mosques will have a place to pray and show the direction of Makkah.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How mosques differ

nodes.misconception: There is only one type of place of worship.
nodes.response: There are many types of places of worship for many religions.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Belonging to a church

nodes.misconception: All Muslims go to Friday prayers at the mosque.
nodes.response: Some Muslims might pray at home.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Belonging to a mosque

nodes.misconception: There is only one type of synagogue.
nodes.response: Synagogues come in different shapes and sizes.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How synagogues differ

nodes.misconception: All Buddhists tend to believe and practice in the same way.
nodes.response: Although there are many common features, there are different forms and expressions of Buddhism in the UK and throughout the world.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Buddha for Buddhists today

nodes.misconception: Meditation is the same as prayer.
nodes.response: Meditation and prayer may both be used to focus the mind, but prayer is usually directed towards God or a god, whereas meditation is not necessarily religious.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Buddha: meditation

nodes.misconception: Buddhists can only be found in Asia.
nodes.response: Buddhism started in Asia, but there are Buddhists throughout the world today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The idea of a Buddha

nodes.misconception: Siddhartha discovered the answer to suffering through fasting.
nodes.response: This did not give him the answer. It was when he stopped being an ascetic and chose the 'middle way' between extreme luxury and extreme self-denial that he found the answer.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Siddhartha: craving and suffering

nodes.misconception: Siddhartha found the way to enlightement through a message from God.
nodes.response: Siddhartha gained enlightenment through meditation.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Siddhartha: enlightenment and impermanence

nodes.misconception: Siddhartha was poor.
nodes.response: Siddhartha was born into a wealthy family and lived in a palace.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Siddhartha: early life

nodes.misconception: That Sunni Muslims believe we have no free will due to predestination, or that Shi'a Muslims believe there is no predestination due to free will.
nodes.response: Most Muslims take a middle ground between them when considering the relationship between free will and predestination in Islam.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Predestination

nodes.misconception: That Shi'a Muslims belive the Imams are Prophets or divine beings in some way.
nodes.response: The Prophet Muhammad was the final prophet and the Imams are not believed to be prophets or divine beings in any way. They were without sin and rightly chosen to lead the community after the death of the final Prophet Muhammad.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Imamah

nodes.misconception: Angels are male (e.g., Jibril is male).
nodes.response: In Islam, angels are genderless but can appear in a male form.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Angels

nodes.misconception: That Prophet Muhammad wrote the words of the Qur'an down once it was revealed to him.
nodes.response: The Prophet Muhammad recited, or said aloud, the words of the Qur'an but this was written down by those who had memorised the revelations.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Seal of the Prophets

nodes.misconception: That Muslims believe Muhammad was the first prophet of Islam.
nodes.response: Muslims belive that Adam was the first prophet of Islam and Muhammad was the final prophet.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Prophethood

nodes.misconception: The six key beliefs are only believed by Sunni Muslims.
nodes.response: Most Muslims (both Sunni and Shia) hold beliefs about tawhid, prophecy, holy books, angels, the Day of Judgement and God's power, but they may not ascribe to them as the 'six articles of faith'.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Six Beliefs of Sunni Islam

nodes.misconception: That the Torah and Gospels in the Jewish and Christian holy texts today are the same as those referenced in the Qur'an.
nodes.response: Muslims believe these have been changed over time from their original form and that the Qur'an corrects those changes.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Holy books

nodes.misconception: That Sevener Shi'a Muslims believe there have only been seven Imams.
nodes.response: The name Sevener comes from the recognition in Sevener Shi'a Islam of Imam Ismail as an Imam. Twelver Shi'a Islam recognises his brother, Musa, as the seventh Imam in contrast.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The five roots of Shi'a Islam

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that Sunni Muslims do not believe in the justice of Allah (Adalat) because it is not mentioned in the six articles of faith.
nodes.response: Al Adl (the just) is one of the 99 Names of Allah and is important to Sunni Muslims as well as Shia, but it isn't in the six articles of faith and may be seen as part of a believe in Tawhid - the oneness of God.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Allah's nature

nodes.misconception: Most Muslims believe in the immortality of the soul but not the body.
nodes.response: The majority of Muslims believe in a physical resurrection.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Judgement and the afterlife

nodes.misconception: Christians believe that Jesus will be the only person to be resurrected.
nodes.response: Many Christians believe that Jesus' resurrection is proof that resurrection is possible for ordinary people in the afterlife.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The afterlife: resurrection

nodes.misconception: The belief in heaven and hell are only important because they help Christians to behave well.
nodes.response: The belief in heaven and hell can guide a Christian's moral behaviour; however, the belief is also important because it can influence Christian attitudes towards death and Christian funeral practices.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Eschatalogical beliefs, heaven and hell

nodes.misconception: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three separate gods.
nodes.response: Most Christians believe in the Oneness of God and that all three Persons of the Trinity are present in only one God, therefore the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three separate gods.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Holy Trinity

nodes.misconception: The means of salvation are grace, Jesus, biblical law and the Holy Spirit, which are distinct and separate from each other.
nodes.response: These concepts are intertwined. Grace can come through Jesus, the law of the Bible and the Holy Spirit.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Sin and salvation

nodes.misconception: Jesus did not suffer during his crucifixion.
nodes.response: The Gospels recall Jesus crying out loudly during his crucifixion, which many Christians interpret as a sign of Jesus' pain.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus Christ: crucifixion

nodes.misconception: Jesus is entirely distinct and separate from God.
nodes.response: For most Christians, Jesus is God in human form. Jesus is both fully human and fully divine.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus Christ: incarnation

nodes.misconception: Christians only follow Jesus' teachings because of their belief in judgement.
nodes.response: Although the Bible makes it clear that there are consequences in the afterlife for actions in this life, for many Christians, the desire to live a good life is rooted in love for God and faith in Jesus as the saviour, not a fear of judgement.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The afterlife: judgement

nodes.misconception: All Christians believe that the Bible is a historical and factual account of history.
nodes.response: Some Christians take a literalist approach and believe that the Bible is a historical and factual account. However, some Christians regard parts of the Bible, including the creation accounts, as metaphorical. This is known as a liberal approach.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Interpretations of Christian creation

nodes.misconception: Each quality or characteristic of God is distinct and separate from the others.
nodes.response: God's qualities and characteristics complement each other. For example, many Christians believe that God exerts his omnipotence with love for humanity, which links to God as (omni)benevolent.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: God's nature

nodes.misconception: There is only one creation story.
nodes.response: Genesis 1 and 2 both tell the story of creation. Genesis 1 focuses on the creation of the universe, and Genesis 2 focuses on the creation of humanity. Genesis 3 is also linked to creation and focuses on The Fall of humanity.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christianity and creation

nodes.misconception: Jesus ascended to heaven immediately after his resurrection.
nodes.response: Jesus ascended to heaven 40 days after his resurrection, according to the New Testament.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus Christ: resurrection and ascension

nodes.misconception: That any religious wedding has the same legal status as a civil one.
nodes.response: Some churches may be able to perform legal marriages, but not all religious marriages are also legal ceremonies.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christianity and relationships in the 21st century

nodes.misconception: That Jesus said that men are the 'head' of the household.
nodes.response: This is recorded in the Bible as being the words of St Paul, not Jesus.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Roles of men and women within relationships

nodes.misconception: That Jesus condemned same sex relationships.
nodes.response: Jesus is not recorded in the Bible speaking in favour or against same sex relationships.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christianity and same sex relationships

nodes.misconception: An annulment is the same as a divorce
nodes.response: An annulment says the marriage was not valid, wheras a divorce ends a marriage.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Divergent Christian views on divorce and marriage

nodes.misconception: All members of a Christian denomination follow all its teachings.
nodes.response: Christians may use their conscience to decide which teachings to follow or not.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian views on sex and contraception

nodes.misconception: That Jesus said 'I do not permit a woman to have authority over a man'
nodes.response: This is attributed to St Paul in the letter to Timothy.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Roles of men and women in Christian worship

nodes.misconception: All Christian weddings are the same.
nodes.response: Christian weddings will vary depending on denomination, cultural/family traditions, etc.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Nature and purpose of marriage

nodes.misconception: That all Christians are against cohabitation.
nodes.response: Some branches of Christianity accept cohabitation if the couple intend to marry.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian attitudes to adultery and cohabitation

nodes.misconception: If humans are capable of moral evil, it means they are inherently evil.
nodes.response: Being capable of moral evil doesn’t mean humans are inherently evil; it suggests that humans have free will and the ability to choose both good and bad actions, depending on circumstances and influences.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The nature of human goodness

nodes.misconception: Kant's deontology means that actions such as killing are always wrong.
nodes.response: The categorical imperative doesn’t mean the same in every situation because it takes the context into account, e.g., killing is generally wrong it can be justified where the intention is to protect life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Deontology and Immanuel Kant

nodes.misconception: Utilitarianism does not argue that any action is acceptable as long as it makes the majority happy.
nodes.response: Utilitarianism considers both the positive and the negative outcomes to determine which action produces the best overall consequences for the greatest number of people.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Teleology and utilitarianism

nodes.misconception: Virtue ethics is just about being nice or kind, so it doesn't require much thought or effort.
nodes.response: Virtue ethics is about developing a well-rounded character through reflection and experience, not just being kind, and requires practising virtues like courage and honesty to achieve flourishing (eudaimonia).
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Virtue ethics

nodes.misconception: Situation ethics allows for any action to be justified as long as it feels loving to the individual.
nodes.response: Situation ethics requires thoughtful consideration and aims for actions that promote selfless and agape love for the well-being of others, rather than justifying actions based on individual feelings.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Situation ethics

nodes.misconception: If we show compassion, we can eliminate suffering entirely.
nodes.response: While compassion can help reduce suffering, it doesn’t always eliminate it, as some suffering may be inevitable or necessary for personal growth and moral development.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Suffering and compassion

nodes.misconception: The two Commandments form part of the Ten Commandments given to Moses by God on Mount Sinai.
nodes.response: The two Commandments are taught by Jesus.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Two great Commandments

nodes.misconception: Halal and haram just applies to food and dietary laws.
nodes.response: Anything that is acceptable or forbidden in Islam is known as halal and haram.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslims and Shariah Law

nodes.misconception: Jesus did not believe people should follow the law.
nodes.response: Jesus believed strongly in the importance of laws and commandments, but that agape love should be used when deciding how to apply those laws and punishments.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Situation ethics of Jesus

nodes.misconception: The Ten Commandments were only relevant at the time, or to people who follow an Abrahamic religion.
nodes.response: The Ten Commandments and other religious rules have influenced many laws still in place, including things such as Sunday trading laws in modern Britain.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Ten Commandments

nodes.misconception: All Muslims think that music is haram or forbidden.
nodes.response: There is a diversity of Islamic worldviews regarding whether music can be listened to and the types of music that are permissible.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Using ijtihad to understand differing Muslim attitudes to music

nodes.misconception: All Muslims will come to the same conclusion about a moral or social issue.
nodes.response: Different scholars will interpret sources differently meaning there is a diversity of opinion about issues such as the Eid moon sighting, and wearing of trousers and beards.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Interpreting Shariah using ijtihad

nodes.misconception: Marriage laws around the world are the same as England & Wales.
nodes.response: Marriage laws vary around the world including minimum age, how many spouses you can have at once, who you can marry and how marriage ceremonies are carried out.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The nature and purpose of marriage

nodes.misconception: All types of contraception work in the same way.
nodes.response: Different types of contraception use different methods, e.g., barrier, hormonal, surgical, intrauterine.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Contraception and family planning

nodes.misconception: That Jesus said 'I do not permit a woman to have authority over a man'
nodes.response: This is attributed to St Paul in the letter to Timothy.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Gender prejudice and discrimination

nodes.misconception: Everyone thinks its okay to have sex before marriage because it's legal in the UK from the age of 16.
nodes.response: Some people do not think that just because it is legal, that it is acceptable. There are reasons why waiting until marriage to have sex is preferred for some people.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Sexual relationships before and outside of marriage

nodes.misconception: That Jesus said that men are the 'head' of the household.
nodes.response: This is recorded in the Bible as being the words of St Paul, not Jesus.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The roles of men and women

nodes.misconception: All members of a Christian denomination follow all its teachings.
nodes.response: Christians may use their conscience to decide which teachings to follow or not.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different religious views about contraception

nodes.misconception: An annulment is the same as a divorce.
nodes.response: An annulment says the marriage was not valid, wheras a divorce ends a marriage.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Religious views about divorce and remarriage

nodes.misconception: There is an ideal family type.
nodes.response: People may have different views on the best types but there is no ideal. All families are different.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The nature of families including the role of parents and children

nodes.misconception: That Jesus condemned same sex relationships.
nodes.response: Jesus is not recorded in the Bible speaking in favour or against same sex relationships.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Human sexuality including heterosexual and same sex relationships

nodes.misconception: Polygamy is only done because men want lots of wives.
nodes.response: There are different types of polygamy (polygyny and polyandry) and there are different reasons why it might be practised.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Contemporary family issues: Polygamy

nodes.misconception: All Christian weddings are the same.
nodes.response: Christian weddings will vary depending on denomination, cultural/family traditions, etc.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Religious attitudes to marriage

nodes.misconception: That liberal Christians do not think the Bible is important for their religion.
nodes.response: Liberal Christians view the Bible as important but will seek to understand it in the context and time that it was written, and are more accepting of modern ideas in relation to their religion than other approaches to Christianity may be.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different religious views about same sex relationships

nodes.misconception: All Christians are against sex before marriage.
nodes.response: Some believe that it is okay if it is between a committed couple, i.e., engaged to marry.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different religious views about sex before marriage

nodes.misconception: Christians think that families are only important for procreation.
nodes.response: Some Christians emphasise that families are important for procreation, but this is not the only purpose of families.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The purpose of families

nodes.misconception: You can divorce for any reason.
nodes.response: Officially, you cannot divorce for any reason. An individual or couple will choose the most appropriate grounds for divorce based on their situation.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Divorce, remarriage and related ethical arguments

nodes.misconception: Each quality or characteristic of God is distinct and separate from the others.
nodes.response: God's qualities and characteristics complement each other. For example, many Christians believe that God exerts his omnipotence with love for humanity, which links to God as (omni)benevolent.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The nature of God

nodes.misconception: The story of Jesus' birth appears in all four of the Gospels.
nodes.response: The story of Jesus' birth is only in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The nativity and Jesus as the son of God

nodes.misconception: There is only one creation story.
nodes.response: Genesis 1 and 2 both tell the story of creation. Genesis 1 focuses on the creation of the universe, and Genesis 2 focuses on the creation of humanity. Genesis 3 is also linked to creation and focuses on the Fall of humanity.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Creation in Genesis

nodes.misconception: Christians ignore the problem of evil and suffering.
nodes.response: Many Christians recognise the problem of evil and suffering in the world, and in their own lives, and respond to the problem by referring to teachings from the Bible.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The problem of evil and suffering

nodes.misconception: Jesus should have used his divine power to avoid his crucifixion.
nodes.response: Jesus went through with the crucifixion because he knew it would bring about a greater good.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The role of Jesus in salvation

nodes.misconception: Jesus ascended immediately after his resurrection.
nodes.response: Jesus ascended into heaven 40 days after his resurrection according to the New Testament.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The resurrection and ascension

nodes.misconception: Christians believe that Jesus will be the only person to resurrect.
nodes.response: Many Christians believe that Jesus' resurrection is proof that resurrection is possible for orindary people in the afterlife.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Beliefs about the afterlife: resurrection

nodes.misconception: Christians do not sin.
nodes.response: Many Christians recognise that humans aren't perfect and sometimes there are times when they will commit sins.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Sin

nodes.misconception: Jesus did not suffer during his crucifixion.
nodes.response: The Gospels recall Jesus crying out loudly during his crucifixion, which many Christians interpret as a sign of Jesus' pain.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The crucifixion of Jesus

nodes.misconception: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three separate gods.
nodes.response: Most Christians believe in the Oneness of God and that all three Persons of the Trinity are present in only one God, therefore the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three separate gods.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Trinity

nodes.misconception: The means of salvation are grace, Jesus, biblical law and the Holy Spirit, which are distinct and separate from each other.
nodes.response: These concepts are intertwined. Grace can come through Jesus, the law of the Bible and the Holy Spirit.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Means of salvation

nodes.misconception: All Christians believe that the Bible is a historical and factual account of history.
nodes.response: Some Christians take a literalist approach and believe that the Bible is a historical and factual account. However, some Christians regard parts of the Bible, including the creation accounts as metaphorical, this is known as a liberal approach.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different Christian interpretations of creation

nodes.misconception: The belief in heaven and hell only influences Christians to behave well.
nodes.response: The belief in heaven and hell can guide a Christian's moral behaviour, however, the belief can also influence Christian attitudes towards death and Christian funeral practices.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Beliefs about the afterlife: heaven and hell

nodes.misconception: Christians only follow Jesus' teachings because of their belief in judgement.
nodes.response: Although the Bible makes it clear that there are consequences in the afterlife for actions in this life, for many Christians, the desire to live a good life is rooted in love for God and faith in Jesus as the saviour, not a fear of judgement.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Beliefs about the afterlife: judgement

nodes.misconception: Jesus is entirely distinct and separate from God.
nodes.response: For most Christians, Jesus is God in human form. Jesus is both fully human and fully divine.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus as the incarnation

nodes.misconception: Jesus should have used his divine power to avoid his crucifixion.
nodes.response: Jesus went through with the crucifixion because he knew it would bring about a greater good.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Salvation and the role of Christ

nodes.misconception: Jesus ascended immediately after his resurrection.
nodes.response: Jesus ascended into heaven 40 days after his resurrection according to the New Testament.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christ's resurrection and ascension

nodes.misconception: Christians believe that Jesus will be the only person to be resurrected.
nodes.response: Many Christians believe that Jesus' resurrection is proof that resurrection is possible for ordinary people in the afterlife.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian eschatology: resurrection

nodes.misconception: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three separate gods.
nodes.response: Most Christians believe in the Oneness of God and that all three Persons of the Trinity are present in only one God, therefore the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three separate gods.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Nature and significance of the Trinity

nodes.misconception: All Christians believe that the Bible is a historical and factual account of history.
nodes.response: Some Christians take a literalist approach and believe that the Bible is a historical and factual account. However, some Christians regard parts of the Bible, including the creation accounts, as metaphorical. This is known as a liberal approach.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Interpreting Genesis

nodes.misconception: The existence of evil and suffering proves that God does not exist.
nodes.response: For Christians, there are a number of Biblical, theoretical and practical responses and solutions to the problem of evil.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The problem of evil

nodes.misconception: There is only one creation story.
nodes.response: Genesis 1 and 2 both tell the story of creation. Genesis 1 focuses on the creation of the universe, and Genesis 2 focuses on the creation of humanity. Genesis 3 is also linked to creation and focuses on the Fall of humanity.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The creation of the universe

nodes.misconception: Jesus is entirely distinct and separate from God.
nodes.response: For most Christians, Jesus is God in human form. Jesus is both fully human and fully divine.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Jesus Christ as the incarnate Son of God

nodes.misconception: The belief in heaven and hell is only important because it influences Christians to behave well.
nodes.response: The belief in heaven and hell can guide a Christian's moral behaviour, however, the belief is also important because it can guide Christian attitudes towards death and Christian funeral practices.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian eschatology: afterlife

nodes.misconception: Christians only follow Jesus' teachings because of their belief in judgement.
nodes.response: Although the Bible makes it clear that there are consequences in the afterlife for actions in this life, for many Christians, the desire to live a good life is rooted in love for God and faith in Jesus as the saviour, not a fear of judgement.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian eschatology: judgement

nodes.misconception: Jesus did not suffer during his crucifixion.
nodes.response: The Gospels recall Jesus crying out loudly during his crucifixion, which many Christians interpret as a sign of Jesus' pain.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The last days of Jesus' life

nodes.misconception: Philosophy is just about saying what you think.
nodes.response: Philosophy does involve thinking hard, but this means critically examining your ideas.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Exploring philosophy

nodes.misconception: Socratic questioning is just about asking difficult questions.
nodes.response: Socratic questioning is a disciplined method of inquiry which includes specific question styles.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Socrates: questioning worldviews

nodes.misconception: Students might think Plato believed we are born knowing everything.
nodes.response: Plato believed learning was a form of remembering knowledge hidden in us.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Plato: exploring worldviews

nodes.misconception: Students might think a blik is a belief or opinion that can be easily changed with evidence.
nodes.response: A blik is a fundamental worldview that is unchanged by evidence or facts.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: R M Hare: worldviews in modern philosophy

nodes.misconception: Socrates, Plato and Aristotle had similar worldviews.
nodes.response: Although Aristotle was Plato's student, he had quite a different worldview and believed we can gain true knowledge by observing the world around us.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Aristotle: applying worldviews

nodes.misconception: Not everyone has a worldview and someone's worldview is entirely their own choice.
nodes.response: We may not be conscious of having a worldview but everyone stands somewhere and our worldview is influenced by many external factors.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Worldviews and religious education

nodes.misconception: Only Roman Catholic Christians go to Lourdes.
nodes.response: Many Roman Catholic Christians do go to Lourdes, but all people, regardless of religion or denomination, are welcome to visit Lourdes.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Pilgrimage to Lourdes

nodes.misconception: Tearfund only responds to large scale disasters.
nodes.response: Tearfund responds to both small scale and large scale disasters.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The work of Tearfund

nodes.misconception: All Christians celebrate the sacraments.
nodes.response: Many Christians do celebrate the sacraments, but not all Christians. For example, Quakers do not celebrate the sacraments.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The sacraments

nodes.misconception: The Bible is only used for reading and recitation during Christian worship.
nodes.response: Reading and reciting Biblical passages can be an important part of Christian worship, but this is not the only use of the Bible during worship. Many Christians interact and engage with the Bible through private reflection or group discussion.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Worship using the Bible

nodes.misconception: The Church is the Christian place of worship.
nodes.response: Church with a capital "C" refers to the community of Christian believers, and church with a lower case "c" refers to the Christian place of worship and often local churches and their congregations.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Church in the local community

nodes.misconception: Christian charities support Christian individuals and communities.
nodes.response: Christian charities, such as CAFOD, support individuals and communities from many different backgrounds all around the world.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The work of CAFOD

nodes.misconception: All Christians celebrate Christmas on the 25th of December.
nodes.response: Some Christians, such as many Eastern Orthodox Christians, celebrate Christmas on the 7th of January.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Celebrating Christmas and Easter

nodes.misconception: Only Christians visit Iona.
nodes.response: Many people visit Iona, including Christians, people who belong to other religions and people with no religion at all. Iona has historical significance as well as religious significance.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Pilgrimage to Iona

nodes.misconception: All Christians worship in the same way.
nodes.response: Worship differs across Christian denominations, with some denominations, such as the Catholic Church, practising liturgical worship, and others, such as the Religious Society of Friends and Pentecostal Churches, practising non-liturgical worship.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Forms of worship

nodes.misconception: Because Christianity is the world's largest religion, Christians do not face persecution.
nodes.response: Christians have been persecuted throughout history and this continues today in some countries where Christianity is a minority religion.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian response to persecution

nodes.misconception: All Christians believe that the bread and wine are symbolic of Jesus' body and blood.
nodes.response: Roman Catholic Christians believe that the substance of the bread and wine becomes Jesus' body and blood during the celebration of the Eucharist; this is known as transubstantiation.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian beliefs about Holy Communion / the Eucharist

nodes.misconception: Evangelism always involves preaching in public.
nodes.response: Evangelism can involve preaching and public speaking, but it can also be carried out through subtle actions and living out the teachings of Jesus in everyday life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Mission, evangelism and Church growth

nodes.misconception: Street Pastors only support the people they directly encounter.
nodes.response: The work of Street Pastors improves the overall safety of local communities.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Street pastors

nodes.misconception: Jesus' death on the cross ended the need for reconciliation.
nodes.response: Reconciliation is still important for many Christians; many Christians believe that the duty to promote reconciliation extends to Christians today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Working for reconciliation

nodes.misconception: Baptism always takes place when a person is a baby/young child.
nodes.response: People can also be baptised when they are adults, this is known as adult baptism and is practised by many Christians.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Christian beliefs about baptism

nodes.misconception: Only people who are religious go on pilgrimage.
nodes.response: Anyone can go on a pilgrimage, whether they are religious or not. However, most pilgrims are religious.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The importance of Walsingham and Taizé

nodes.misconception: Evangelism always involves preaching in public.
nodes.response: Evangelism can involve preaching and public speaking, but it can also be carried out through subtle actions and living out the teachings of Jesus in everyday life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Evangelism, mission and Church growth

nodes.misconception: All Christians celebrate Christmas on the 25th of December.
nodes.response: Some Christians, such as many Eastern Orthodox Christians, celebrate Christmas on the 7th of January.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: How Christians celebrate Christmas and Easter

nodes.misconception: Jesus' death on the cross ended the need for reconciliation.
nodes.response: Reconciliation is still important for many Christians; many Christians believe that the duty to promote reconciliation extends to Christians today.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Reconciliation

nodes.misconception: All people belong to some form of religion.
nodes.response: According to the 2021 Census in England and Wales, there are an increasing number of individuals who have no religion.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The census and Christianity in the UK

nodes.misconception: The Church is the Christian place of worship.
nodes.response: Church with a capital "C" refers to the community of Christian believers, and church with a lower case "c" refers to the Christian place of worship and often local churches and their congregations.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Church and the local community

nodes.misconception: All Christians celebrate baptism and the Eucharist in the same way.
nodes.response: Many Christians celebrate baptism and the Eucharist, however, this can happen in many different ways. For example, there are different beliefs regarding the age that baptism takes place, and different beliefs and interpretations about the Eucharist.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Role, meaning and celebration of baptism and the Eucharist

nodes.misconception: All Christians worship in the same way.
nodes.response: Worship differs across Christian denominations, with some denominations, such as the Catholic Church, practising liturgical worship, and others, such as the Religious Society of Friends and Pentecostal Churches, practising non-liturgical worship.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different forms of worship

nodes.misconception: Because Christianity is the world's largest religion, Christians do not face persecution.
nodes.response: Christians have been persecuted throughout history and this continues today in some countries where Christianity is a minority religion.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Persecution of Christians: past and present

nodes.misconception: All Christians celebrate the sacraments.
nodes.response: Many Christians do celebrate the sacraments, but not all Christians. For example, Quakers do not celebrate the sacraments.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Diverse beliefs regarding sacraments

nodes.misconception: That reaching heaven by faith alone means that works and deeds do not matter in that understanding of Christianity.
nodes.response: Good works and deeds are still important even though they do not help a person reach heaven. In this understanding of Christianity, these actions and deeds come about because of faith and show the faith is genuine.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Reaching heaven by faith alone

nodes.misconception: Vandana Shiva opposes all types of farming.
nodes.response: Vandana Shiva supports farming methods which respect nature and biodoversity.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Vandana Shiva: protecting the earth

nodes.misconception: Bonhoeffer was an absolute pacifist for his whole life.
nodes.response: Bonhoeffer was a pacifist, but had the opportunity to help with the attempt to assassinate Hitler, which he decided he should try to do, given the great evil and injustice Hitler was causing.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Dietrich Bonhoeffer, the pacifist

nodes.misconception: The laws of a country are always based on fairness and equality.
nodes.response: Sometimes the laws of a country are not fair or just, for example, Apartheid and segregation were supported by laws in the USA and South Africa.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Fighting against unjust laws

nodes.misconception: Ahimsa only refers to non-violence towards humans.
nodes.response: Ahimsa refers to non-violence towards all living things, as all living things have value, worth and are interconnected.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Dharma, Bhumi and the environment

nodes.misconception: That Martin Luther King was an important figure in the Protestant Reformation.
nodes.response: Martin Luther King lived in the 20th century, but was named after Martin Luther who lived in the 16th century when the Protestant Reformation happened.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Martin Luther and the Reformation

nodes.misconception: Christianity and evolution are completely incompatible.
nodes.response: Many Christian denominations accept evolution as part of God's creative process, including the Catholic Church and the Church of England.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The relationship between religious and scientific views on the origin of life

nodes.misconception: Christians believe life on earth is unimportant because the afterlife is what truly matters.
nodes.response: While Christians believe in an afterlife, they still see life on earth as valuable. It is God-given and is an opportunity to do good (Matthew 25:40). Their actions in this life have eternal consequences.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Impact of beliefs about death and the afterlife on the value of human life

nodes.misconception: Dominion is the opposite of stewardship.
nodes.response: Dominion is seen as authority or power, but, in common with stewardship, it is usually seen as including a duty to be responsible.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The value of the world and stewardship

nodes.misconception: All Christians interpret the Genesis creation story literally.
nodes.response: Many Christians see Genesis as metaphorical or compatible with scientific explanations, such as theistic evolution.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Religious teachings about the origins of life

nodes.misconception: All Christians believe the same thing about abortion.
nodes.response: In reality, views vary between denominations, with the Catholic Church strongly opposing abortion, while the Church of England and Methodists allow it in some cases.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different religious views about abortion

nodes.misconception: Those with non-religious views, such as Humanists, always support euthanasia.
nodes.response: Many Humanists advocate for the right to die (e.g., ‘Dignity in Dying’), but some oppose it due to concerns about coercion, vulnerable people, or better alternatives like palliative care.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Euthanasia

nodes.misconception: Animal experimentation always harms animals.
nodes.response: While animal experimentation can involve harm, modern practices aim to minimise suffering by using alternatives, reducing the number of animals used, and refining procedures to ensure humane treatment.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different religious views about animal experimentation

nodes.misconception: All Christians see the sanctity of life as a moral absolute.
nodes.response: Different denominations and individuals may have varying perspectives on whether extrinsic factors such as dignity or well-being impinge on the sanctity of life.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Sanctity of life

nodes.misconception: Christians within the same tradition or denomination have the same views on using animals for food.
nodes.response: In reality, even within the same denomination, Christians can have different views based on personal beliefs, scripture interpretations and culture. Some follow official teachings, while others make their own ethical choices.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The use of animals for food

nodes.misconception: Quality of life is about reducing suffering.
nodes.response: Quality of life means different things to different people. Whilst it can be about reducing suffering, it is influenced by individual values, preference and circumstances.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Quality of life

nodes.misconception: All Christians completely oppose euthanasia.
nodes.response: While many Christian strongly oppose euthanasia, some take a more compassionate approach, considering quality of life and situation ethics. Some may support assisted dying in certain circumstances, though this remains a minority view.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Different religious views about euthanasia

nodes.misconception: The Big Bang theory and Genesis 1-2 cannot be reconciled.
nodes.response: Many Christians see the Big Bang as part of God’s creation.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Religious teachings about the origin of the universe

nodes.misconception: Abortion debates are always clearly pro-life vs. pro-choice.
nodes.response: Many positions are more nuanced, e.g., some people who identify as pro-life accept abortion in certain circumstances, and some who are pro-choice may personally oppose abortion but support the legal right to choose.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Ethical arguments related to abortion

nodes.misconception: All Christians believe in heaven and hell as literal places.
nodes.response: Some Christians interpret them metaphorically as states of being, such as being in God's presence or being separated from God.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Beliefs about death and the afterlife

nodes.misconception: Global citizenship is not just about helping others in distant communities.
nodes.response: It involves recognising our interconnectedness with people and the planet, meaning that the actions we take in our everyday lives have a far-reaching impact. Global citizens take personal responsibility for their own environmental practices.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The use and abuse of the environment

nodes.misconception: Everyone in the Torah or Old Testament always believed in only one god.
nodes.response: Abram's family and the people of Abram's homeland were polytheists, meaning they believed in multiple gods.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The world of Abram

nodes.misconception: Covenants are only found in the Old Testament or Torah.
nodes.response: Many covenants are found in the Old Testament or Torah, but the new covenant is contained within the New Testament.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Meaning and examples of covenants

nodes.misconception: All Abrahamic religions believe that Jesus is the New covenant.
nodes.response: Jesus as the New covenant is central to Christian belief. Most Jews do not believe that Jesus is the New covenant. In Islam, Jesus is considered a prophet.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The New covenant

nodes.misconception: All Jews, Christians and Muslims practice circumcision because of the Abrahamic covenant.
nodes.response: Not everyone who follows an Abrahamic faith will practice circumcision because of the Abrahamic covenant. Jews, Christians and Muslims place differing levels of importance on the religious practice of circumcison.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Becoming Abraham

nodes.misconception: The promised lands are only significant within Judaism.
nodes.response: The promised lands are significant for different reasons within the three Abrahamic religions.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The promised lands

nodes.misconception: Judaism, Christianity and Islam have nothing in common.
nodes.response: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are Abrahamic faiths and all three religions can be traced back to Abraham through his sons Ishmael and Isaac and their descendants.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Father of many nations

nodes.misconception: Islam teaches that people are born sinful or evil.
nodes.response: Islam teaches that all people are born pure (in a state of fitrah), and have the ability to choose between right and wrong.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim teachings about good, evil and suffering

nodes.misconception: All Muslims support harsh punishments.
nodes.response: While these punishments are mentioned in the Qur’an as part of hudud, most Muslims believe they can only be applied under very strict conditions by proper Islamic authorities. Mercy, forgiveness and reform are key values in Islamic justice.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim attitudes towards punishment

nodes.misconception: Islamic views on punishment are primarily focused on retribution.
nodes.response: In Islam, justice is the central aim of punishment, and retribution is only one way of achieving it. The Qur’an allows for qisas (equal retaliation), but it also encourages forgiveness, mercy and the opportunity for repentance and reform.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Islam and the aims of punishment

nodes.misconception: All Muslim countries follow Islamic law exactly as it is in the Qur’an.
nodes.response: In reality, some Muslim-majority countries mix Islamic principles with national laws, and not all follow the Qur’an’s teachings fully, especially on justice and human rights.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Islam and the treatment of criminals

nodes.misconception: Prison chaplains just lead services and prayers.
nodes.response: Prison chaplains provide pastoral care, support rehabilitation and emotional wellbeing, help with faith-based education and often work with other organisations to support resettlement and reintegration. They also assist prisoners of all or no faiths.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: The Muslim Chaplains Association and Mosaic

nodes.misconception: Islam teaches that all crimes are equally wrong.
nodes.response: Islam teaches that crimes should be judged fairly, based on harm, intention and context. Serious crimes like murder are treated more severely, while causes like poverty or illness may affect how a crime is viewed.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim attitudes towards crime

nodes.misconception: Forgiveness in Islam means the offender is not punished.
nodes.response: Islam allows for both justice and forgiveness. An offender may still face consequences, but forgiveness is encouraged when there is sincere taubah and efforts to make amends.
nodes.subject: religious-education
nodes.lessonTitle: Muslim teachings about forgiveness:

nodes.misconception: In Islam, justice is always focused on punishment.
nodes.response: Islam teaches justice must be fair and include mercy. Offenders who repent can be forgiven. It's about responsibility and change, not just punishment.
nodes.subject: religious-education
